subject: SOC2 re-attestation: evidence retainer & renewal playbook
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@brightline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC2 re-attestation: evidence retainer & renewal playbook

Hi Evan / Priya,

Thanks again for the productive phone yesterday. As Brightline moves toward renewal in January, we'd like to propose a lightweight "evidence retainer" workflow to reduce lift on your side during the SOC2 re-attestation window and to preserve the 365d retention carve that your compliance team requested.

High-level proposal (attached):
- We’ll stage incremental evidence (logs, control artifacts) into a secured GDrive folder on a weekly cadence starting 2026-12-06.
- Redwood will maintain a read-only snapshot of audit logs for a 365d retention window; any deviation (short-term carveouts) will be flagged and captured in the retention diff PDF.
- For renewal, we suggest a 3-week evidence sprint (Dec 13–31) with a prefunded retainer credit to cover verification and export costs.

Action items for Brightline:
1) Confirm acceptance of the retainer approach and carveout window by 2026-12-03.
2) Provide a primary compliance contact (we have Evan and Priya listed).
3) Sign the attached SLA amendment to reflect the retention carve and burst capacity for evidence exports. (DocuSign link to follow once legal approves).

I've attached a proposed SOC2_evidence_index.xlsx with the suggested cadence and the log-retention-carveout-diff.pdf that highlights what changes on our end vs your requested carveout.

If useful, Ben and Kim are looped to confirm capacity & credits. Happy to run a 30-min kickoff this week.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0181

Attachments: SOC2_evidence_index.xlsx, log-retention-carveout-diff.pdf

From: Evan Li <evan.li@brightline.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightline.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC2 re-attestation: evidence retainer & renewal playbook

Priya —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifying Qs from our InfoSec team after I reviewed the attachments:
- For the 365d retention snapshot, can Redwood support an immutable export (S3 Glacier) if we request a legal hold?
- How do burst costs scale if we need on-demand full snapshots for our auditors (we’ll likely need 2 exports during the sprint)?
- Can the retainer be applied to offset overage charges when the burst occurs, or does it only cover verification labor?

We can confirm the primary compliance owner after our internal check — likely Priya Shah. We want to avoid an SLA amendment with ambiguous billing for burst exports.

Can Kimberly/Ben comment on the burst pricing model?

Thanks,
Evan
Director, Information Security
Brightline Financial
ev an.li@brightline.com

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 09:12, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message and attachments]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC2 re-attestation: evidence retainer & renewal playbook

Folks —

Short answers to Evan’s questions:
- Immutable export: yes, we can stage an immutable export to an S3 bucket with Glacier Deep Archive lifecycle. That is handled as an "export job" and includes integrity checks.
- Burst pricing: export jobs are priced by GB exported + request overhead. For planning, assume ~€0.08/GB exported for long-term archive export plus a $350 flat job orchestration fee. (I’ll add exact USD rates on the live sheet).
- Retainer use: retainer credits can be applied to orchestration and verification labor; we can also structure it to offset a capped portion of export fees if Brightline prefers — suggest cap of $5k per sprint in the amendment.

Ben / Priya: do we want to propose the capped offset in the SLA amendment or keep the retainer strictly for labor and bill export fees separately? If the goal is to preserve Brightline’s predictable renewal economics, capping export offsets is cleaner for the customer.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: updated_pricing_line_items.csv (referenced in drive)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@brightline.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC2 re-attestation: evidence retainer & renewal playbook

Evan / Priya,

Appreciate the quick review. We can do the capped offset approach — proposed language below for the amendment (we’ll ask legal to translate into the SLA doc):

- "Retainer credits will be applied first to labor and verification tasks associated with evidence staging and extraction. Up to $5,000 per evidence sprint may be applied against export job fees (storage + egress). Export fees beyond the capped amount will be billed at standard export rates)."

Proposed timeline (firm):
- 2026-12-03: Brightline confirms primary compliance contact + approves capped-offset approach.
- 2026-12-06: Weekly evidence staging begins.
- 2026-12-13 through 2026-12-31: Evidence sprint window (two potential export jobs).
- 2027-01-10: Target date for SOC2 re-attestation submission.

Marissa is looped for billing language and any renewal credits; Ben can validate operational runbook (exports + snapshots).

If you’re comfortable with the amended language, I’ll push the Draft SLA amendment (DocuSign) by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks —
Priya

Attachments: (referenced) SOC2_evidence_index.xlsx, log-retention-carveout-diff.pdf

From: Evan Li <evan.li@brightline.com>
